findings.evidence: Location rows 'Inside a repository, no scope stated' and 'Inside a repository, user says "for the team"...' both resolve to `.claude/commands/<name>.md`; the second row restates the default the model would already infer
findings.fix: Merge the two rows into one: 'Inside a repository, unless the user says global or personal | `.claude/commands/<name>.md`'

findings.evidence: Frontmatter and Arguments sections are fact tables ('`arguments: file lines` makes `$file`, `$lines`') with no decision prompt for choosing named arguments, `$0` or whole `$ARGUMENTS`
findings.fix: Add one 'Before choosing placeholders, ask:' line: free text that may contain spaces -> `$ARGUMENTS` whole; one or more fixed-shape values -> named `arguments:` so the body can test for empty; never `$1` for the first value

findings.evidence: Two silent-failure facts sit outside Gotchas: 'a skill with the same name wins and the command is silently unused' (line 13) and 'broken YAML loads the body with no fields and no error' (line 59)
findings.fix: Add both as Gotchas bullets with their consequence, e.g. 'A same-named skill in .claude/skills/ or ~/.claude/skills/ shadows the command with no warning: check before writing' and 'Frontmatter not starting on line 1 or invalid YAML is silently dropped, including disable-model-invocation'

findings.evidence: Queries are terse and formal ('Create a reusable `/deploy-preview` slash command for this project.'); none has file paths, typos or backstory, and few positives describe the need without saying 'command'
findings.fix: Rewrite 3-4 positives as realistic implicit-need prompts (e.g. 'every friday i do git pull, bump package.json, npm publish, post in #releases, can i just type one thing for that?') and add context such as paths and team names to near-miss negatives

findings.evidence: 'a skill with the same name wins and the command is silently unused' states the check but not the branch outcome when a same-named skill exists
findings.fix: Add the branch: 'If one exists, stop and offer to rename the command (suggest `<name>-cmd` or a namespaced path) or to update the skill instead; never write a shadowed command'
